text:
alex: Quick sync — the RFC suggested moving canary/A-B decisioning to a central policy service. main worry: single-point-of-decision and availability. thoughts?

jamie: I think split policy vs enforcement. policy returns a plan + TTL lease, routers enforce locally. that avoids synchronous dependency for every request.

taylor: Lease makes sense. also need a "dead-man" fallback: if router loses contact with policy, default back to a safe route (stable) instead of trying to guess.

sam: Agree. policy should include a failure-mode field. e.g. { fail_mode: stable | degraded | partial, plan_id, ttl_ms, actions:[{variant, weight}] }
maria: Also: router should emit decision_source, plan_id, lease_expiry to telemetry. add metric rollout_decision_age_ms so we can see staleness.
deploy-bot: deploy initiated: rollout/feature-x canary -> 10% at 12:22 UTC :rocket:
alex: Edge-case: frequent policy churn. routers should cache until TTL or explicit invalidation push. TTLs must be conservative for critical tenants.
jamie: Implementation sketch: policy API proposal and router pseudo-behavior: 
```
POST /v1/decisions 
body: { app, env, variant, constraints }
resp: { plan_id, actions:[{ route: "stable", weight: 90 },{ route: "canary", weight: 10 }], ttl_ms: 300000, fail_mode: "stable" }
```
Router pseudo: 
```
decision = cache.get(plan_key)
if not decision:
  decision = call(policy)
  cache.set(plan_key, decision, ttl_ms)
if router.can_contact_policy():
  enforce(decision.actions)
else:
  // policy unreachable
  if decision and !decision.expired:
    enforce(decision.actions) // use cached plan
  else:
    enforce(stable_route) // dead-man fallback
```

taylor: One more: atomicity and cache-coherence. when switching weights we must avoid stomping session-affinity / KV caches. add optional per-action flags: warmup=true/drain=true so downstream can prepare.
sam: And local heuristics are useful: router could observe error_rate/latency and proactively shift weight even if policy reachable (local safe fallback). important for emergent issues that policy doesn't know about.
maria: Ops playbook suggestion: emit alerts when decision TTLs are expiring and policy unreachable for >2x TTL. escalate to pager if >5 minutes. include plan_id in pager so oncall can correlate.
alex: :thumbsup: good direction. I'll draft RFC follow-up with: policy schema, router behavior, TTL semantics, telemetry keys, and playbook. any objections to me taking this on?
jamie: go for it, please include per-tenant overrides and enterprise SLA semantics.
taylor: add a short perf note: cache hit avoids extra RTT per request but increases memory/eviction pressure on routers — need bounds.
sam: small note: make sure canary weights respond smoothly (no big jumps) and respect required warmup time.
maria: I'll add dashboards for decision_age, policy_call_failures, and plan_expiry_count.
alex: thanks all — i'll post a draft in #architecture-rfcs and ping when ready. :white_check_mark:
